## Question

[CAI-248](<https://linear.app/caiuswang/issue/CAI-248>) explicitly parked this until the row was known — "pagination and filtering stay in the map's fog until the row is known" — and the row is now known: one query, all keys, **0.9 ms cold / 0.12 ms warm for 21 rows** on the live 1.74 GB database, ordered by **most recent activity descending**. So this ticket inherits a settled row and a settled order, and decides only what surrounds them.

* **Pagination.** The measured population is **21 keys**, growing at roughly one per linked task. `SkillReadsView.vue`'s keyset cursor is the precedent, but it exists for a table of a different order of magnitude. At what count does an unpaginated list actually fail — and is building a cursor now for a list of 21 the kind of speculative machinery `CLAUDE.md` scope control refuses? If it is deferred, does the endpoint's shape still have to leave room for it, or is adding a cursor later a clean change?
* **Filtering, and what it would be filtering *for*.** The candidates are not equal: `stage`, `has open defects`, `has escapes`, `has sessions`, `unattributed only`. Measured today, **open defects and escapes are 0 for all 21 keys**, so two of those filters select nothing — and a filter chip that always yields an empty list teaches the operator the data is broken.
* The **one filter that would bite today** separates the **16 keys with a task link** from the **5 known only from a defect**. But [CAI-248](https://linear.app/caiuswang/issue/CAI-248/what-a-feature-index-is-and-how-features-are-enumerated) ruled those five are the *most* informative rows in the list, so a filter that hides either group works against the reason the index exists. Is "provenance" a filter, or a visible property of the row and nothing more?
* **Search.** With 21 keys, `⌘F` is the search. With 200, it is not. Is a key/title substring filter the cheaper answer to both this and pagination — the list stays whole and the user narrows it — given the whole query is 0.12 ms and could re-run on every keystroke without a debounce?
* Does any of this reach the **URL**? A filtered index that cannot be linked to is a filtered index nobody shares.

The constraint that governs all of it: [CAI-248](https://linear.app/caiuswang/issue/CAI-248/what-a-feature-index-is-and-how-features-are-enumerated) fixed the cost of a row at **one query for the whole page, no per-row query and no packet**. A filter or a cursor that reintroduces per-row work has broken the index, whatever it adds.
